# Overview

The sample info file uses two `colony_id` formats depending on timepoint:

| Timepoint | Format | Example |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| T0 | `{site}_{coral}_{timepoint}_R{rep}` | `JC_40_T0_R1` |
| T1+ | `{site}{coral}_{timepoint}_R{rep}` | `JC40_T2_R1` |

The data files use a different format with replicate and timepoint swapped, the `R` prefix dropped, and the replicate zero-padded:

| Target format | Example |
|---------------|---------|
| `{site}_{coral}_{rep}_{timepoint}` | `JC_40_01_T0` |

This script parses the original IDs and creates a standardised `colony_id` column that matches the data files.

# Read sample info

```{r read}
sample_info <- read_csv("data/master_sample_info.csv") 
```

# Create colony_id

A single regex with an optional `_?` between site and coral number handles both input formats.

```{r transform}
sample_info <- sample_info %>%
  extract(
    original_id,
    into   = c("site", "coral", "timepoint", "rep"),
    regex  = "^([A-Z]+)_?([0-9]+)_(T[0-9]+)_R([0-9]+)$",
    remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    colony_id = paste(site, coral, sprintf("%02d", as.integer(rep)), timepoint, sep = "_")
  ) 
```

# Spot-check

One row per timepoint to verify the transformation.

```{r spot-check}
sample_info %>%
  group_by(monitoring) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(original_id, colony_id, monitoring)
```

# Check for parse failures

Any rows where the regex did not match will have `NA` in `colony_id`.

```{r check-na}
failures <- sample_info %>% filter(is.na(colony_id))

if (nrow(failures) == 0) {
  cat("No parse failures — all", nrow(sample_info), "rows matched successfully.\n")
} else {
  warning(nrow(failures), " row(s) failed to parse:")
  print(failures)
}
```

Check for duplicates
```{r}
# Check for duplicate original_id in sample_info
dupes <- sample_info %>% filter(duplicated(original_id))
if (nrow(dupes) > 0) {
  warning(nrow(dupes), " duplicate original_id(s) found in sample_info:")
  print(dupes)
} else {
  cat("No duplicate original_ids found in sample_info.\n")
}

```


# Write output

```{r write}
write_csv(sample_info, "data/sample_info_colony_id.csv")
cat("Saved", nrow(sample_info), "rows to data/sample_info_colony_id.csv\n")
```
